Paracetamol.uses: Temporary relief of certain mild pain and fever.
Paracetamol.age: Age-specific use depends on the exact product and strength. Follow the product label.
Paracetamol.precautions: Do not exceed the labeled amount. Check combination cold/flu medicines for duplicate paracetamol.
Paracetamol.sideEffects: Usually tolerated when used correctly. Overdose can cause serious liver injury.
Paracetamol.interactions: Some medicines and combination products may contain the same active ingredient.
Paracetamol.status: Commonly available OTC in many markets.
Paracetamol.warning: Do not use more than directed.

Ibuprofen.purpose: NSAID pain reliever and fever reducer
Ibuprofen.uses: Temporary relief of certain pain, inflammation and fever.
Ibuprofen.age: Age restrictions vary by product. Follow the exact label.
Ibuprofen.precautions: People with certain stomach, kidney, heart or other conditions may need professional advice.
Ibuprofen.sideEffects: May cause stomach upset and other adverse effects.
Ibuprofen.interactions: Can interact with certain blood thinners and other NSAIDs.
Ibuprofen.food: Follow the product label; some people take it with food to reduce stomach upset.
Ibuprofen.status: OTC in many markets, but availability varies.
Ibuprofen.warning: Do not combine with another NSAID unless advised.

Dolo 650.uses: Temporary relief of fever and mild to moderate pain such as headache, body aches, muscle pain and toothache.
Dolo 650.dose: 650 mg per tablet. Do not use this entry as a personalized dosing calculator. Follow the exact package label or advice from a doctor/pharmacist; age, weight, liver health and other medicines can affect safe use.
Dolo 650.age: Generally intended for adults and adolescents when appropriate. Dose for children should be based on age/weight and medical guidance.
Dolo 650.precautions: Use caution in people with liver disease, heavy alcohol use, malnutrition, or those taking other medicines containing paracetamol. Follow the recommended dose.
Dolo 650.sideEffects: Usually well tolerated when used correctly. Possible side effects include nausea, stomach discomfort or allergic reactions. Serious liver damage can occur with overdose.
Dolo 650.interactions: May interact with medicines such as warfarin and other medicines containing paracetamol. Avoid taking multiple paracetamol-containing products together.
Dolo 650.food: Can be taken with or without food.
Dolo 650.status: OTC medicine in India, subject to applicable local regulations.
Dolo 650.warning: Do not exceed the recommended daily amount. Do not combine Dolo 650 with other medicines containing paracetamol unless advised by a healthcare professional. Seek medical advice if fever is persistent, severe, or accompanied by concerning symptoms.

Cetirizine.uses: Relief of certain allergy symptoms such as sneezing, itching and runny nose.
Cetirizine.precautions: May cause drowsiness in some people.
Cetirizine.sideEffects: Drowsiness, tiredness or dry mouth may occur.
Cetirizine.interactions: Other medicines that cause drowsiness may increase this effect.
Cetirizine.food: Usually can be taken with or without food; follow the label.
Cetirizine.warning: Do not drive or operate machinery if it makes you drowsy.

Loratadine.age: Follow the exact product's age directions.
Loratadine.sideEffects: Headache, tiredness or dry mouth may occur.
Loratadine.interactions: Tell a pharmacist or doctor about other medicines.
Loratadine.warning: Seek urgent care for severe allergic reactions.

Omeprazole.uses: Reduces stomach acid and is used for certain acid-related conditions.
Omeprazole.age: Age and duration depend on the exact product and condition.
Omeprazole.precautions: Persistent or recurrent symptoms should be medically evaluated.
Omeprazole.sideEffects: Headache, nausea or abdominal symptoms can occur.
Omeprazole.interactions: Can interact with some prescription and non-prescription medicines.
Omeprazole.food: Product directions may specify timing in relation to meals.
Omeprazole.status: OTC or prescription depending on product and country.
Omeprazole.warning: Do not use longer than the product label recommends without medical advice.

Antacid.uses: Temporary relief of heartburn and acid indigestion.
Antacid.sideEffects: Some products may cause constipation or diarrhea.
Antacid.interactions: Some antacids can affect absorption of other medicines.
Antacid.warning: Persistent or severe chest or abdominal symptoms require medical evaluation.

ORS.uses: Helps replace fluids and electrolytes lost through diarrhea or vomiting.
ORS.age: Use an age-appropriate product and follow preparation instructions.
ORS.precautions: Prepare exactly according to the package directions.
ORS.sideEffects: Incorrect preparation can cause inappropriate electrolyte intake.
ORS.interactions: Medical conditions affecting fluid balance may require professional advice.
ORS.food: Used as a fluid replacement rather than a conventional tablet medicine.
ORS.warning: Severe dehydration or inability to drink requires urgent medical care.

Dextromethorphan.precautions: Do not exceed labeled directions. Check combination cough/cold products.
Dextromethorphan.sideEffects: Drowsiness, dizziness or nausea can occur.
Dextromethorphan.interactions: Can interact with some medicines, including certain serotonergic medicines.
Dextromethorphan.warning: Persistent or worsening cough requires medical evaluation.

Saline Nasal Spray.uses: Helps moisturize the nose and loosen nasal mucus.
Saline Nasal Spray.warning: Persistent severe nasal symptoms require evaluation.

Clotrimazole.uses: Used for certain superficial fungal skin infections.
Clotrimazole.age: Age suitability depends on the product and treatment area.
Clotrimazole.precautions: For external use according to product instructions.
Clotrimazole.sideEffects: Local irritation or redness may occur.
Clotrimazole.interactions: Ask a pharmacist if using other topical medicines on the same area.
Clotrimazole.warning: Persistent or worsening rash should be professionally evaluated.

Hydrocortisone.uses: May reduce inflammation and itching in certain skin conditions.
Hydrocortisone.age: Use in children and on sensitive areas according to professional/product guidance.
Hydrocortisone.precautions: Do not use on an undiagnosed infection without appropriate advice.
Hydrocortisone.sideEffects: Skin irritation can occur; prolonged inappropriate use can thin skin.
Hydrocortisone.interactions: Tell a healthcare professional about other topical medicines.
Hydrocortisone.status: OTC or prescription depending on strength and country.
Hydrocortisone.warning: Worsening redness, pain, pus or fever may indicate infection.

Benzoyl Peroxide.precautions: Can cause dryness and irritation. Avoid eyes.
Benzoyl Peroxide.interactions: Other irritating skin products can increase irritation.
Benzoyl Peroxide.warning: Stop and seek advice for severe irritation or allergic reaction.

Loperamide.uses: May reduce diarrhea in appropriate situations.
Loperamide.precautions: Do not use for certain bloody or infectious diarrhea without medical advice.
Loperamide.sideEffects: Constipation, abdominal discomfort or nausea may occur.
Loperamide.interactions: Ask a pharmacist about other medicines.
Loperamide.warning: Blood in stool, high fever or severe abdominal pain requires medical evaluation.

Salbutamol Inhaler.uses: Relieves wheezing and shortness of breath by relaxing airway muscles.
Salbutamol Inhaler.age: Age-specific use depends on the exact product. Follow the product label.
Salbutamol Inhaler.precautions: Often prescription-only; asthma should be diagnosed and monitored by a doctor.
Salbutamol Inhaler.sideEffects: Tremor, rapid heartbeat or nervousness may occur.
Salbutamol Inhaler.interactions: Certain heart medicines and other bronchodilators may interact.
Salbutamol Inhaler.status: Prescription or pharmacist-supervised in many markets.
Salbutamol Inhaler.warning: Seek urgent care if breathing difficulty is severe or not relieved.

Simethicone.uses: Relieves bloating and discomfort caused by excess gas.
Simethicone.food: Usually taken after meals; follow the label.
Simethicone.warning: Persistent bloating or pain should be medically evaluated.

Psyllium Husk (Isabgol).uses: Helps relieve constipation and supports regular bowel movements.
Psyllium Husk (Isabgol).precautions: Take with adequate water to avoid choking or blockage.
Psyllium Husk (Isabgol).sideEffects: Bloating or gas, especially when starting use.
Psyllium Husk (Isabgol).interactions: May affect absorption of some medicines if taken at the same time.
Psyllium Husk (Isabgol).food: Usually mixed with water or milk; follow the label.
Psyllium Husk (Isabgol).warning: Persistent constipation should be medically evaluated.

Bisacodyl.uses: Provides short-term relief of occasional constipation.
Bisacodyl.precautions: Not intended for long-term regular use.
Bisacodyl.interactions: Ask a pharmacist about use with other medicines.
Bisacodyl.warning: Persistent or severe constipation requires medical evaluation.

Domperidone.uses: Used for relief of nausea and vomiting.
Domperidone.age: Age restrictions apply; follow product label or medical advice.
Domperidone.precautions: May be prescription-only in some countries due to heart-rhythm concerns.
Domperidone.sideEffects: Rarely, heart rhythm changes; dry mouth or headache may occur.
Domperidone.interactions: Can interact with certain heart and other medicines.
Domperidone.food: Usually taken before meals; follow the label.
Domperidone.status: OTC or prescription depending on country.
Domperidone.warning: Persistent vomiting or signs of dehydration require medical care.

Ketoconazole Shampoo.uses: Helps reduce flaking and itching associated with dandruff.
Ketoconazole Shampoo.precautions: For external scalp use only; avoid contact with eyes.
Ketoconazole Shampoo.sideEffects: Scalp irritation or dryness may occur.
Ketoconazole Shampoo.interactions: Few known interactions with topical use.
Ketoconazole Shampoo.warning: Persistent or worsening scalp irritation should be evaluated.

Lubricating Eye Drops.uses: Soothes eye irritation, dryness and discomfort.
Lubricating Eye Drops.age: Generally suitable for most ages; follow the label.
Lubricating Eye Drops.precautions: Does not treat infection; bacterial conjunctivitis needs prescription drops.
Lubricating Eye Drops.sideEffects: Mild, temporary blurring or stinging may occur.
Lubricating Eye Drops.warning: Eye pain, vision change or thick discharge needs prompt medical evaluation.

Iron Supplement.uses: Used to address iron-deficiency related low blood counts.
Iron Supplement.age: Follow the product-specific label or medical advice.
Iron Supplement.precautions: Best confirmed by a doctor with a blood test before long-term use.
Iron Supplement.sideEffects: Constipation, dark stools or stomach upset may occur.
Iron Supplement.interactions: Can reduce absorption of some other medicines if taken together.
Iron Supplement.food: Often taken with food to reduce stomach upset; follow the label.
Iron Supplement.warning: Keep out of reach of children; iron overdose can be dangerous.

Folic Acid.uses: Supports red blood cell production, often alongside iron for anemia.
Folic Acid.age: Follow the product-specific label or medical advice.
Folic Acid.precautions: Usually well tolerated at standard doses.
Folic Acid.interactions: Ask a pharmacist about use with certain other medicines.
Folic Acid.food: Can usually be taken with or without food.
Folic Acid.warning: Underlying cause of anemia should be medically evaluated.

Vitamin D3 Supplement.uses: Addresses vitamin D deficiency and supports bone health.
Vitamin D3 Supplement.age: Follow the product-specific label or medical advice.
Vitamin D3 Supplement.precautions: Very high doses over time can cause toxicity.
Vitamin D3 Supplement.interactions: Ask a pharmacist about use with certain other medicines.
Vitamin D3 Supplement.food: Often taken with a meal for better absorption.
Vitamin D3 Supplement.warning: Confirm deficiency and dosing with a healthcare professional.

Vitamin B12 Supplement.uses: Addresses vitamin B12 deficiency, supporting nerve and blood health.
Vitamin B12 Supplement.age: Follow the product-specific label or medical advice.
Vitamin B12 Supplement.precautions: Severe deficiency may need injections under medical supervision.
Vitamin B12 Supplement.interactions: Ask a pharmacist about use with certain other medicines.
Vitamin B12 Supplement.food: Can usually be taken with or without food.
Vitamin B12 Supplement.warning: Confirm deficiency and dosing with a healthcare professional.

Multivitamin.uses: May help support general energy and nutritional levels.
Multivitamin.precautions: Not a substitute for evaluating the underlying cause of persistent fatigue.
Multivitamin.interactions: Ask a pharmacist about use with certain other medicines.
Multivitamin.warning: Persistent fatigue should be medically evaluated.

Melatonin.uses: May help with occasional difficulty falling asleep.
Melatonin.age: Availability and age restrictions vary by country; follow the label.
Melatonin.precautions: Not regulated as OTC in all countries; check local status.
Melatonin.sideEffects: Drowsiness, headache or dizziness may occur.
Melatonin.interactions: May interact with certain other medicines; ask a pharmacist.
Melatonin.status: OTC in some markets, prescription-only in others.
Melatonin.warning: Persistent insomnia should be medically evaluated.

Dimenhydrinate.uses: Helps prevent and relieve motion sickness symptoms.
Dimenhydrinate.age: Age restrictions vary by product; follow the label.
Dimenhydrinate.precautions: May cause drowsiness; avoid driving or operating machinery.
Dimenhydrinate.sideEffects: Drowsiness, dry mouth or blurred vision may occur.
Dimenhydrinate.interactions: Other sedating medicines may increase drowsiness.
Dimenhydrinate.food: Usually taken before travel; follow the label.
Dimenhydrinate.warning: Consult a doctor before use in young children.

Diclofenac Gel.uses: Local relief of muscle, joint and sprain-related pain and swelling.
Diclofenac Gel.age: Usually for adults and older adolescents; follow the exact product label.
Diclofenac Gel.precautions: Apply only to intact skin. Avoid eyes, mouth and broken skin. Wash hands after use. Use caution if you have asthma triggered by NSAIDs, or stomach, kidney or heart problems.
Diclofenac Gel.sideEffects: Local skin redness, itching or irritation. Rarely, allergic reactions.
Diclofenac Gel.interactions: Avoid using together with oral NSAIDs unless advised. Tell a professional if you take blood thinners.
Diclofenac Gel.status: OTC in many markets; strength and availability vary.
Diclofenac Gel.warning: Do not apply under tight bandages or heat pads unless the label allows.

Pain Relief Balm / Spray.ingredient: Counter-irritants such as menthol, methyl salicylate or camphor
Pain Relief Balm / Spray.purpose: Topical muscle and joint pain relief
Pain Relief Balm / Spray.uses: Temporary warming or cooling relief for minor muscle aches, stiffness and sprains.
Pain Relief Balm / Spray.age: Not for young children; check the label for the minimum age.
Pain Relief Balm / Spray.precautions: Use only on intact skin. Avoid eyes, mucous membranes and open wounds. Do not use with heating pads. Methyl salicylate products can be risky for people allergic to aspirin or on blood thinners.
Pain Relief Balm / Spray.interactions: Methyl salicylate may add to the effect of blood thinners if used over large areas.
Pain Relief Balm / Spray.warning: Keep out of reach of children; swallowing can be toxic.

Aspirin.purpose: NSAID pain reliever and fever reducer
Aspirin.uses: Temporary relief of mild to moderate pain such as headache.
Aspirin.age: Generally not for children or teenagers with fever or viral illness (risk of Reye's syndrome).
Aspirin.precautions: Avoid in people with stomach ulcers, bleeding disorders, asthma triggered by NSAIDs, or in late pregnancy unless a doctor advises. Do not start daily low-dose use without medical advice.
Aspirin.sideEffects: Stomach irritation or bleeding, heartburn, easy bruising, allergic reactions.
Aspirin.interactions: Interacts with blood thinners, other NSAIDs, some diabetes and blood pressure medicines.
Aspirin.food: Taking with food may reduce stomach upset.
Aspirin.status: OTC in many markets; availability varies.
Aspirin.warning: Do not combine with another NSAID unless advised. Do not give to children or teens for fever.

Famotidine.uses: Relief and prevention of heartburn and acid indigestion.
Famotidine.age: Check label; not for young children without medical advice.
Famotidine.precautions: People with kidney problems may need professional advice. Seek care if heartburn is frequent, severe or comes with trouble swallowing, weight loss or black stools.
Famotidine.interactions: May affect absorption of some medicines (e.g., certain antifungals and HIV medicines).
Famotidine.food: Can be taken with or without food; follow the label.
Famotidine.status: OTC in some markets; prescription-only in others.

Levocetirizine.uses: Relief of sneezing, runny nose, itching and watery eyes from allergies; itchy skin.
Levocetirizine.age: Age-specific forms exist; follow the label or a doctor's advice.
Levocetirizine.precautions: May cause drowsiness in some people. Use caution with kidney problems. Avoid alcohol and driving if drowsy.
Levocetirizine.interactions: Additive sedation with alcohol or sedative medicines.
Levocetirizine.food: Can be taken with or without food.
Levocetirizine.status: Availability varies by country; commonly sold OTC in India.
Levocetirizine.warning: Do not combine with other antihistamines unless advised.

Fexofenadine.uses: Relief of sneezing, runny nose, itchy or watery eyes and itching from allergies.
Fexofenadine.age: Age-specific strengths exist; follow the label.
Fexofenadine.sideEffects: Headache, nausea, dizziness; drowsiness is uncommon.
Fexofenadine.interactions: Antacids with aluminium/magnesium and fruit juices (grapefruit, orange, apple) can reduce absorption.
Fexofenadine.food: Take with water; avoid fruit juice around the dose.
Fexofenadine.status: OTC in many markets; availability varies.
Fexofenadine.warning: Do not take with fruit juice.

Chlorpheniramine.form: Tablet / Syrup (often in combination cold products)
Chlorpheniramine.uses: Relief of sneezing, runny nose and itching from colds and allergies.
Chlorpheniramine.age: Not suitable for very young children; follow the label.
Chlorpheniramine.precautions: Causes drowsiness. Use caution with glaucoma, enlarged prostate, urinary retention, or if driving. Check combination products for duplicate ingredients.
Chlorpheniramine.sideEffects: Drowsiness, dry mouth, blurred vision, urinary difficulty.
Chlorpheniramine.interactions: Additive sedation with alcohol, sleeping pills or other antihistamines.
Chlorpheniramine.food: Can be taken with or without food.
Chlorpheniramine.status: Commonly OTC, often as part of combination cold medicines.
Chlorpheniramine.warning: Do not drive or operate machinery if drowsy.

Xylometazoline Nasal Spray.uses: Short-term relief of blocked nose from colds, sinusitis or allergies.
Xylometazoline Nasal Spray.age: Child-strength products differ; follow the label.
Xylometazoline Nasal Spray.precautions: Use only for the short period stated on the label (usually a few days). Caution with high blood pressure, heart disease, thyroid disease or glaucoma.
Xylometazoline Nasal Spray.sideEffects: Nasal dryness, stinging, sneezing. Longer use can cause rebound congestion.
Xylometazoline Nasal Spray.warning: Prolonged use can worsen congestion (rebound effect).

Guaifenesin.form: Syrup / Tablet (often in combination cough products)
Guaifenesin.uses: Relief of chest congestion with thick mucus.
Guaifenesin.age: Check the label; not suitable for young children in many products.
Guaifenesin.precautions: Drink plenty of fluids. Seek care if cough lasts more than about a week, or comes with fever, rash, persistent headache or breathlessness.
Guaifenesin.sideEffects: Nausea, vomiting, dizziness or stomach upset.
Guaifenesin.interactions: Check combination products for duplicate ingredients.
Guaifenesin.food: Take with water; follow the label.

Ambroxol.uses: Helps clear mucus in productive cough and bronchitis.
Ambroxol.age: Pediatric forms exist; follow the label or doctor's advice.
Ambroxol.precautions: Use caution with stomach ulcers or severe liver/kidney disease. Stop and seek care if skin reactions occur.
Ambroxol.sideEffects: Nausea, stomach upset, taste changes. Rare allergic or skin reactions.
Ambroxol.interactions: Usually few interactions; avoid combining with cough suppressants unless advised.
Ambroxol.status: Commonly sold OTC or on pharmacist advice in India; varies elsewhere.
Ambroxol.warning: Do not use with cough suppressants without advice.

Throat Lozenges.uses: Temporary relief of sore throat and throat irritation.
Throat Lozenges.age: Not suitable for young children (choking risk); follow the label.
Throat Lozenges.precautions: Check ingredients if you have allergies or diabetes (sugar content). Seek care if sore throat is severe, lasts over a few days or comes with high fever.
Throat Lozenges.sideEffects: Mouth irritation or numbness; rare allergic reactions.
Throat Lozenges.interactions: Avoid doubling up with other products containing the same active ingredient.
Throat Lozenges.food: Dissolve slowly; avoid eating or drinking right after if numbing.
Throat Lozenges.warning: Persistent sore throat needs medical evaluation.

Calamine Lotion.uses: Relieves itching and irritation from insect bites, heat rash, mild sunburn and minor skin rashes.
Calamine Lotion.age: Generally suitable across ages when used on skin; check the label.
Calamine Lotion.precautions: Do not apply to broken or severely blistered skin, or near the eyes. Stop if irritation worsens.
Calamine Lotion.interactions: No significant interactions when applied to skin.

Povidone-Iodine.uses: Cleaning minor cuts, scrapes and wounds to reduce infection risk.
Povidone-Iodine.age: Use with care in infants; follow the label.
Povidone-Iodine.precautions: Do not use on deep wounds, serious burns or animal bites without medical advice. Avoid with iodine allergy or thyroid disorders and avoid long or large-area use.
Povidone-Iodine.interactions: May be inactivated by some other antiseptics; can affect thyroid tests.
Povidone-Iodine.warning: For external use only; do not swallow.

Terbinafine Cream.uses: Treats athlete's foot, ringworm and jock itch.
Terbinafine Cream.precautions: Keep the area clean and dry. Complete the full course even if symptoms fade. Avoid eyes and mouth. See a doctor if no improvement or if nails/scalp are involved.
Terbinafine Cream.sideEffects: Mild itching, burning or redness at the application site.
Terbinafine Cream.interactions: No significant interactions expected with topical use.

Permethrin.age: Age restrictions vary; follow the label or doctor's advice.
Permethrin.precautions: Follow the label exactly; household contacts and bedding may also need treatment. Avoid eyes and broken skin. Itching can persist for weeks after successful treatment.
Permethrin.sideEffects: Temporary itching, burning, redness or tingling.
Permethrin.interactions: No significant interactions expected with topical use.
Permethrin.status: OTC in some markets; may need a prescription in others.
Permethrin.warning: Do not use on infants without medical advice.

Albendazole.age: Use in young children only as directed by a doctor.
Albendazole.precautions: Avoid in pregnancy unless a doctor advises. People with liver disease need medical guidance. Household hygiene and treating close contacts matter.
Albendazole.interactions: Some medicines (e.g., certain anticonvulsants, cimetidine) can change its levels.
Albendazole.food: Often taken with food (especially fatty food) to improve absorption; follow instructions.
Albendazole.status: Prescription status varies; commonly dispensed on pharmacist or doctor advice.
Albendazole.warning: Seek medical advice before use in pregnancy or for children.

Hyoscine Butylbromide.uses: Relief of abdominal cramps and spasms, including with IBS.
Hyoscine Butylbromide.age: Usually for adults and older children; follow the label.
Hyoscine Butylbromide.precautions: Avoid with glaucoma, enlarged prostate, urinary retention, myasthenia gravis or bowel obstruction. Seek care for severe or persistent abdominal pain.
Hyoscine Butylbromide.sideEffects: Dry mouth, dizziness, fast heartbeat, constipation.
Hyoscine Butylbromide.interactions: Additive effect with other anticholinergic medicines such as some antihistamines.
Hyoscine Butylbromide.food: Can be taken with or without food.
Hyoscine Butylbromide.status: OTC in some markets, prescription-only in others.
Hyoscine Butylbromide.warning: Severe abdominal pain, fever or blood in stool needs medical care.

Probiotics.ingredient: Live beneficial bacteria or yeast (e.g., Lactobacillus, Bifidobacterium, Saccharomyces)
Probiotics.uses: May help with some types of diarrhea and with digestive symptoms such as IBS or bloating.
Probiotics.precautions: People with weakened immunity, central lines or serious illness should consult a doctor first. Effects vary between strains and products.
Probiotics.interactions: Take apart from antibiotics unless the label says otherwise; antifungal medicines may reduce yeast-based probiotics.
Probiotics.status: Sold as supplements or food products.
Probiotics.warning: Not a substitute for fluids (ORS) in diarrhea.

Zinc Supplement.uses: Used with ORS in children's diarrhea under medical guidance, and for zinc deficiency.
Zinc Supplement.age: Pediatric dosing should follow medical guidance or label.
Zinc Supplement.precautions: Do not exceed the labeled amount; high intake can cause copper deficiency. Can cause nausea on an empty stomach.
Zinc Supplement.interactions: Can reduce absorption of some antibiotics (quinolones, tetracyclines) and iron.
Zinc Supplement.food: Taking with food may reduce stomach upset.
Zinc Supplement.warning: Do not exceed the labeled amount.

Calcium Supplement.ingredient: Calcium carbonate or citrate (often with vitamin D3)
Calcium Supplement.uses: Helps meet calcium needs when diet is not enough.
Calcium Supplement.age: Follow the label for age-appropriate products.
Calcium Supplement.precautions: Avoid excess; people with kidney stones, high blood calcium or kidney disease need medical advice.
Calcium Supplement.interactions: Can reduce absorption of some antibiotics, thyroid medicine and iron; separate by a few hours.
Calcium Supplement.food: Calcium carbonate is best with food; calcium citrate can be taken any time.
Calcium Supplement.warning: Do not exceed the labeled amount.

Chlorhexidine Mouthwash.uses: Helps reduce plaque and gum inflammation (gingivitis) and supports mouth hygiene.
Chlorhexidine Mouthwash.age: Not for young children who may swallow it; follow the label.
Chlorhexidine Mouthwash.precautions: Do not swallow. Typically for short-term use; can stain teeth or tongue. See a dentist for persistent gum problems.
Chlorhexidine Mouthwash.sideEffects: Teeth or tongue staining, temporary taste change, mouth irritation.
Chlorhexidine Mouthwash.interactions: Some toothpastes may reduce its effect; rinse mouth between brushing and mouthwash.
Chlorhexidine Mouthwash.food: Avoid eating or drinking right after use.
Chlorhexidine Mouthwash.warning: Not a replacement for brushing and dental care.

Oral Pain Relief Gel.ingredient: Choline salicylate / benzocaine / lidocaine (varies by product)
Oral Pain Relief Gel.purpose: Topical mouth ulcer and gum pain relief
Oral Pain Relief Gel.uses: Temporary relief of pain from mouth ulcers and minor gum irritation.
Oral Pain Relief Gel.age: Salicylate-containing gels are generally not for young children; follow the label.
Oral Pain Relief Gel.precautions: Apply a small amount with clean hands. See a doctor or dentist if ulcers last more than about 2–3 weeks or recur often.
Oral Pain Relief Gel.interactions: Avoid if allergic to aspirin or local anesthetics.
Oral Pain Relief Gel.food: Avoid eating or drinking right after application.
Oral Pain Relief Gel.warning: Do not use on large areas or for long periods.

Carbamide Peroxide Ear Drops.uses: Helps soften and loosen earwax buildup.
Carbamide Peroxide Ear Drops.age: Not for infants; follow the label.
Carbamide Peroxide Ear Drops.precautions: Do not use if you have ear pain, discharge, a perforated eardrum, or ear surgery history. Do not use cotton buds or sharp objects to remove wax.
Carbamide Peroxide Ear Drops.sideEffects: Mild irritation, fizzing sensation, temporary muffled hearing.
Carbamide Peroxide Ear Drops.warning: See a doctor if pain, discharge or hearing loss occurs.

Aloe Vera Gel.uses: Soothes mild sunburn and minor first-degree burns once the skin is cooled.
Aloe Vera Gel.age: Generally suitable across ages when used on skin.
Aloe Vera Gel.precautions: For mild burns, cool the area with running water first. Use pure or cosmetic-grade gel; avoid on open wounds or blistered skin. Patch-test if sensitive.
Aloe Vera Gel.interactions: No significant interactions with topical use.
Aloe Vera Gel.status: Widely available as a cosmetic/OTC product.
Aloe Vera Gel.warning: Seek medical care for large, deep, blistering or face/genital burns.

Emollient / Moisturizer.ingredient: Petrolatum, glycerin, ceramides, liquid paraffin or similar
Emollient / Moisturizer.uses: Relieves dry, flaky or itchy skin and supports eczema and psoriasis care.
Emollient / Moisturizer.age: Suitable across ages; choose fragrance-free products for sensitive skin.
Emollient / Moisturizer.precautions: Apply generously and often, ideally after bathing. Patch-test if prone to allergies. Paraffin-based products can be flammable on fabrics.
Emollient / Moisturizer.sideEffects: Occasional stinging or rash from fragrances or preservatives.
Emollient / Moisturizer.interactions: May reduce absorption of other creams if applied immediately before them.
Emollient / Moisturizer.warning: Keep away from open flames if using paraffin-based products.

Acyclovir Cream.uses: Reduces duration of cold sores (herpes labialis) when started at the first tingle.
Acyclovir Cream.precautions: Use on lips and face only; avoid eyes and inside the mouth. Wash hands after use. Contagious until healed. See a doctor if sores are frequent or severe.
Acyclovir Cream.interactions: No significant interactions with topical use.
Acyclovir Cream.status: OTC in some markets; prescription in others.
Acyclovir Cream.warning: Do not share towels or touch sores.

Salicylic Acid.uses: Helps treat acne, warts and thickened skin.
Salicylic Acid.age: Check label; avoid on infants and very large areas in children.
Salicylic Acid.precautions: Avoid broken or inflamed skin, face for wart products, and eyes. Can cause dryness and peeling. Do not use on diabetic foot ulcers or with poor circulation without medical advice.
Salicylic Acid.interactions: Avoid combining with other strong exfoliants or retinoids unless advised.
Salicylic Acid.warning: For external use only; stop if burning or severe irritation occurs.

Sunscreen.ingredient: UV filters (SPF 30 or higher, broad spectrum)
Sunscreen.uses: Helps prevent sunburn and sun damage.
Sunscreen.age: Babies under 6 months should be kept out of direct sun; follow pediatric advice.
Sunscreen.precautions: Apply generously and reapply as directed, especially after sweating or swimming. Patch-test if you have sensitive skin.
Sunscreen.sideEffects: Skin irritation or breakouts in some people.
Sunscreen.warning: Sunscreen reduces but does not eliminate risk; use shade and clothing too.

Lactulose.age: Use in children only as directed by label or doctor.
Lactulose.precautions: Can cause gas and cramps. Avoid in people with galactose intolerance; use caution with diabetes. Seek care for constipation with severe pain, vomiting or blood in stool.
Lactulose.sideEffects: Bloating, gas, abdominal cramps, loose stools.
Lactulose.interactions: Other laxatives may add to effects.
Lactulose.food: Follow the label; drink adequate fluids.
Lactulose.warning: Prolonged laxative use should be medically supervised.

Menthol Vapor Balm.uses: Gives a cooling sensation that helps with feeling of blocked nose from colds.
Menthol Vapor Balm.age: Not for infants or very young children (check label, often not under 2–3 years).
Menthol Vapor Balm.precautions: Apply externally to chest/neck as directed; do not apply to broken skin, nostrils or face of young children. Avoid contact with eyes. Do not heat or microwave.
Menthol Vapor Balm.sideEffects: Skin irritation; vapors may irritate airways, especially in asthma.
Menthol Vapor Balm.interactions: No significant interactions with external use.
Menthol Vapor Balm.warning: Camphor is toxic if swallowed; keep away from children.
